source.original_text: For each real Euclidean natural dimension n>=2, take F(x)=log(norm x) if n=2 and F(x)=norm(x)^(2-n) if n>2. These literal source functions are harmonic on the entire complement of0. Expanding the source omitted boundary calculations: for every R>0 and every x with norm(x)=R, F(x) equals log R in n=2 and R^(2-n) in n>2, while the pairing of its actual gradient with R inverse times x is R inverse in n=2 and (2-n)*R^(1-n) in n>2. All exponents use real subtraction. The all-radius bundle is ASTIS expansion, not a numbered HFT theorem; no distributional normalization, geometric normal or integral identity is asserted.

lean.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ}, 2 ≤ n →
    let F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x =>
      if n = 2 then Real.log ‖x‖ else ‖x‖ ^ ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ))
    InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd F ({0}ᶜ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) ∧
    ∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), ‖x‖ = R →
      F x = (if n = 2 then Real.log R else R ^ ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ))) ∧
      inner ℝ (gradient F x) (R⁻¹ • x) =
        (if n = 2 then R⁻¹ else ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ)) * R ^ ((1 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ)))
decoder_context: EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard l2 norm and inner product.
gradient is the Riesz representative of the actual Fréchet derivative; Laplacian.laplacian is the orthonormal trace of the actual second Fréchet derivative.
ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g s means that g is twice continuously real-differentiable locally at the scalar point s. Scalar deriv denotes the ordinary real derivative.
InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd f s means: at every x in s, f is locally C2 and its actual Euclidean Laplacian vanishes on a neighborhood of x.

The set {0}ᶜ is the complement of the singleton origin. Real.log is the real logarithm, and a real exponent uses real rpow. Only positive norms occur in the asserted punctured-domain and positive-sphere conclusions.

reconstruction.text: For every natural number n ≥ 2, let E = ℝⁿ with its standard Euclidean inner product and norm, and define F: E → ℝ by F(x) = log ‖x‖ if n = 2 and F(x) = ‖x‖^(2 − n) otherwise, with the latter power interpreted as a real power. Then F is harmonic on a neighborhood of each point of E ∖ {0}: at every x ≠ 0, F is locally C² and its actual Euclidean Laplacian vanishes throughout some neighborhood of x. Moreover, for every real radius R > 0 and every x ∈ E satisfying ‖x‖ = R, both F(x) = log R if n = 2 and F(x) = R^(2 − n) if n ≥ 3, and ⟨∇F(x), R⁻¹x⟩ = R⁻¹ if n = 2 and ⟨∇F(x), R⁻¹x⟩ = (2 − n)R^(1 − n) if n ≥ 3. The gradient is the Riesz representative of the actual Fréchet derivative, and R⁻¹x is the outward radial unit vector on that sphere. Dimension expressions in real exponents and coefficients use the real value of n. No harmonicity, regularity, or sphere identity is asserted at the origin or for a nonpositive radius.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Calculus.RadialCalculus
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Harmonic.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Deriv
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Deriv

/-!
The literal power/log Green test functions used in HFT, second edition,
printed pages 2 and 5 (PDF pages 10 and 13). The source omits these calculus
computations. The all-positive-radius boundary formula below is an explicit
ASTIS expansion. No distributional normalization, geometric annulus normal,
Green identity, zero flux or mean-value theorem is claimed here.
-/

open Filter
open scoped Topology RealInnerProductSpace
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Harmonic.FundamentalSolution
set_option autoImplicit false
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Calculus.RadialCalculus
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]

omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] in
private theorem power_sq_profile (q : ℝ) :
    (fun z : E => ‖z‖ ^ q) = (fun z : E => (‖z‖ ^ 2) ^ (q / 2)) := by
  funext z
  rw [← Real.rpow_natCast, ← Real.rpow_mul (norm_nonneg _)]
  congr 1
  ring

private theorem power_data (q : ℝ) (x : E) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun z : E => ‖z‖ ^ q) x ∧
    gradient (fun z : E => ‖z‖ ^ q) x = (q * ‖x‖ ^ (q - 2)) • x ∧
    Laplacian.laplacian (fun z : E => ‖z‖ ^ q) x =
      q * (q + (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) - 2) * ‖x‖ ^ (q - 2) := by
  have hn : ‖x‖ ≠ 0 := norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr hx
  have hS : ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hn
  let p : ℝ := q / 2
  have hc : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun s : ℝ => s ^ p) (‖x‖ ^ 2) :=
    Real.contDiffAt_rpow_const_of_ne hS
  have hb := radial_gradient_laplacian (fun s : ℝ => s ^ p) (0 : E) x (by simpa using hc)
  simp only [sub_zero, Real.deriv_rpow_const', deriv_const_mul_field,
    Real.deriv_rpow_const] at hb
  have hp : (‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1) = ‖x‖ ^ (q - 2) := by
    rw [← Real.rpow_natCast, ← Real.rpow_mul (norm_nonneg _)]
    congr 1
    dsimp [p]
    ring
  have he : (‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 2) * (‖x‖ ^ 2) = (‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1) := by
    rw [← Real.rpow_add_one hS]
    congr 1
    ring
  refine ⟨(contDiffAt_id.norm ℝ hx).rpow_const_of_ne hn, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [power_sq_profile q]
    convert hb.1 using 1
    rw [hp]
    congr 1
    dsimp [p]
    ring
  · rw [power_sq_profile q]
    calc
      _ = 4 * (‖x‖ ^ 2) * (p * ((p - 1) * (‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1 - 1))) +
          2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) * (p * (‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1)) := hb.2
      _ = (2 * p * (2 * p + (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) - 2)) *
          (‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1) := by
        rw [show p - 1 - 1 = p - 2 by ring]
        calc
          _ = 4 * p * (p - 1) * ((‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 2) * (‖x‖ ^ 2)) +
              2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) * p * (‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1) := by ring
          _ = _ := by rw [he]; ring
      _ = _ := by rw [hp]; dsimp [p]; ring

omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] in
private theorem log_sq_profile :
    (fun z : E => Real.log ‖z‖) = (fun z : E => (1 / 2 : ℝ) * Real.log (‖z‖ ^ 2)) := by
  funext z
  rw [Real.log_pow]
  ring

private theorem log_data (x : E) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun z : E => Real.log ‖z‖) x ∧
    gradient (fun z : E => Real.log ‖z‖) x = (‖x‖ ^ 2)⁻¹ • x ∧
    Laplacian.laplacian (fun z : E => Real.log ‖z‖) x =
      ((Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) - 2) * (‖x‖ ^ 2)⁻¹ := by
  have hn : ‖x‖ ≠ 0 := norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr hx
  have hS : ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hn
  have hc : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun s : ℝ => (1 / 2 : ℝ) * Real.log s) (‖x‖ ^ 2) :=
    contDiffAt_const.mul (Real.contDiffAt_log.mpr hS)
  have hb := radial_gradient_laplacian (fun s : ℝ => (1 / 2 : ℝ) * Real.log s)
    (0 : E) x (by simpa using hc)
  simp only [sub_zero, deriv_const_mul_field', Real.deriv_log', deriv_const_mul_field,
    deriv_inv] at hb
  refine ⟨(contDiffAt_id.norm ℝ hx).log hn, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [log_sq_profile]
    convert hb.1 using 1
    congr 1
    ring
  · rw [log_sq_profile, hb.2]
    field_simp [hS]
    ring

/-- HFT's power/log test functions are harmonic away from the origin, with
their literal values and outward radial derivative on every positive sphere.
The all-radius bundle expands computations omitted by the source. -/
theorem fundamentalSolution_boundary_data {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    let F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun x =>
      if n = 2 then Real.log ‖x‖ else ‖x‖ ^ ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ))
    InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd F ({0}ᶜ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) ∧
    ∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), ‖x‖ = R →
      F x = (if n = 2 then Real.log R else R ^ ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ))) ∧
      inner ℝ (gradient F x) (R⁻¹ • x) =
        (if n = 2 then R⁻¹ else ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ)) * R ^ ((1 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ))) := by
  dsimp only
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hn with hdim | hdim
  · have hdim : n = 2 := hdim.symm
    simp only [hdim, ↓reduceIte]
    constructor
    · intro x hx
      have hne : x ≠ 0 := by simpa using hx
      refine ⟨(log_data x hne).1, ?_⟩
      filter_upwards [eventually_ne_nhds hne] with z hz
      simpa [hdim] using (log_data z hz).2.2
    · intro R hR x hx
      have hne : x ≠ 0 := norm_ne_zero_iff.mp (by rw [hx]; exact hR.ne')
      refine ⟨by rw [hx], ?_⟩
      rw [(log_data x hne).2.1]
      simp only [real_inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hx]
      field_simp
  · have hdim : n ≠ 2 := ne_of_gt hdim
    simp only [hdim, ↓reduceIte]
    constructor
    · intro x hx
      have hne : x ≠ 0 := by simpa using hx
      refine ⟨(power_data ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ)) x hne).1, ?_⟩
      filter_upwards [eventually_ne_nhds hne] with z hz
      simp [(power_data ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ)) z hz).2.2]
    · intro R hR x hx
      have hne : x ≠ 0 := norm_ne_zero_iff.mp (by rw [hx]; exact hR.ne')
      refine ⟨by rw [hx], ?_⟩
      rw [(power_data ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ)) x hne).2.1]
      simp only [real_inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hx]
      have he : R ^ ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ) - 2) * R = R ^ ((1 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ)) := by
        rw [← Real.rpow_add_one hR.ne']
        congr 1
        ring
      calc
        _ = ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ)) * (R ^ ((2 : ℝ) - (n : ℝ) - 2) * R) := by
          field_simp
        _ = _ := by rw [he]
end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Harmonic.FundamentalSolution

notation.text: Squared radius, arbitrary intermediate real power, and the explicit outward radial unit vector.

steps.title: Use the literal source functions away from their pole
steps.text: Positive norm at a nonzero point allows smooth logarithms and real powers on a neighborhood. Rewrite the literal radial functions using squared radius; the identities hold as functions, so they legitimately transfer derivatives.
steps.lean: power_sq_profile and log_sq_profile prove the function identities. power_data and log_data derive actual local C2 internally using norm, log and rpow calculus.

steps.title: Compute the actual power derivatives
steps.text: Apply the canonical radial formula with scalar profile S raised to q/2, and use the positive-radius real-power identity to combine exponents.
steps.lean: power_data calls RadialCalculus.radial_gradient_laplacian. Real.deriv_rpow_const and Real.rpow_add_one supply the explicit scalar derivatives and simplifications.

steps.title: Compute the logarithmic derivatives separately
steps.text: Apply the same canonical node to one half of log S. Its first two scalar derivatives give the logarithmic gradient and Laplacian. The source logarithmic case is not obtained from the degenerate power with exponent zero.
steps.lean: log_data calls the same radial_gradient_laplacian and uses deriv_const_mul_field, Real.deriv_log and deriv_inv. Nonzero squared norm discharges all denominator conditions.

steps.title: Join the two dimension cases and conclude harmonicity
steps.text: If n=2, the logarithmic Laplacian vanishes. If n>2, substituting q=2-n makes the power coefficient zero. Each nonzero point has a neighborhood avoiding the pole, so these pointwise calculations give a zero-Laplacian germ alongside actual local C2.
steps.lean: fundamentalSolution_boundary_data splits eq_or_lt_of_le hn and uses eventually_ne_nhds with the full private data bundles. HarmonicOnNhd contains both C2 and neighborhood zero Laplacian.

steps.title: Evaluate on a positive-radius sphere
steps.text: Substitute norm x=R into the literal values. Pair the actual gradient with R inverse times x. The inner product contributes R inverse times R squared, producing the stated radial derivatives. No surface integral or geometric normal theorem is used.
steps.lean: The final quantified boundary conclusion uses real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, the private gradient formulas and Real.rpow_add_one with positive R.

lesson.lean_statement: The only external premise is the source dimension. Positive-radius and sphere conditions are guards inside the boundary conclusion.
lesson.lean_proof: Both literal cases use internally derived local C2 and the same canonical radial node; no theorem about Green integrals is assumed.
